topics.name: Cells and their parts
misconceptions: Learners think plant and animal cells are exactly the same, or that animal cells have chloroplasts.

topics.name: Photosynthesis and respiration
misconceptions: Learners think plants only make food and never release energy from it, or that respiration is the same as breathing.

topics.name: Atoms, elements and the periodic table
misconceptions: Learners think atoms can be seen with the naked eye, or that an element is the same as a compound.

topics.name: Chemical reactions and word equations
prerequisites: Atoms, elements and the periodic table
misconceptions: Learners think matter is lost or created during a reaction, or that every reaction needs fire or heat.

topics.name: Acids, bases and the pH scale
misconceptions: Learners think every acid is deadly to touch, that bases are always safe, or that neutral means pH zero.

topics.name: Reproduction in flowering plants
misconceptions: Learners think flowers cannot make seeds without help from people, or that pollination and fertilisation are the same step.

topics.name: Electric circuits
misconceptions: Learners think electricity gets used up as it goes around, or that a bigger battery always makes a bulb brighter.

topics.name: Heat transfer
misconceptions: Learners think cold is something that moves, or that metal is naturally colder than other materials.

topics.name: Rocks and the rock cycle
misconceptions: Learners think rocks stay the same forever, or that all rocks formed at the same time.

topics.name: Weather and climate
misconceptions: Learners confuse weather with climate, or think one hot day proves the climate is changing.

topics.name: Ecosystems and food webs
misconceptions: Learners think top predators are outside the food web, or that decomposers do not matter.

topics.name: Human impact on the environment
misconceptions: Learners think their own actions cannot harm the environment, or that pollution is only what you can see.

topics.name: The solar system and the seasons
misconceptions: Learners think seasons happen because Earth moves closer to or farther from the Sun, or that the Sun orbits Earth.

topics.name: Forces and motion graphs
misconceptions: Learners think a downward sloping graph means moving backwards, or that no forces act on an object that is not moving.
